subject: general
question: If the simple interest on a sum of money at 8% per annum in 2 years is ₹2,000, find the compound interest on the same sum for the same period at the same rate in case of annual compounding.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The effective **Simple Interest** rate for 2 years at 8% = 8 + 8 = 16%.

The effective **Compound Interest** rate for 2 years = 8 + 8 + (8 × 8) ÷ 100 = 16.64%.

Given that 16% corresponds to ₹2,000.

Required **Compound Interest** (16.64%) = (2000 ÷ 16) × 16.64

⇒ 125 × 16.64 = ₹2080.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹2080.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Simple Interest** (SI) = ₹2,000 | **Rate** (R) = 8% p.a. | **Time** (T) = 2 years

**Formula Used:**

SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

CI for 2 years = SI + (Interest on 1st year SI)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a765e7a3069baa49f8eddd56e6b9f310fd609a10868c22f303a700e081091021.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 2000 = (P × 8 × 2) ÷ 100

⇒ 2000 = 16P ÷ 100

⇒ P = (2000 × 100) ÷ 16

⇒ P = ₹12,500

⇒ SI for 1st year = 2000 ÷ 2 = ₹1000

⇒ **Compound Interest** (CI) = SI for 2 years + (8% of 1st year SI)

⇒ CI = 2000 + (1000 × 8 ÷ 100)

⇒ CI = 2000 + 80 = ₹2080

**∴ The correct answer is ₹2080.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Effective Rate of CI

For 2 years, the effective interest rate can be calculated using the successive percentage formula: R + R + (R × R) ÷ 100.

Difference between CI and SI

The difference (D) between CI and SI for 2 years is given by the formula: D = P × (R ÷ 100)².

General CI Formula

Amount (A) = P(1 + R ÷ 100)ⁿ, where n is the number of years. CI = A − P.
